svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "Where is the receptor? It depends on the ligand."], [1, "Transmembrane receptor: hydrophobic in the membrane, hydrophilic either side."], [2.5, "A hydrophilic ligand binds it and stays outside the cell."], [6, "A hydrophobic steroid passes through the membrane..."], [8.5, "...and binds an intracellular receptor in the cytoplasm."], [10.5, "The complex moves into the nucleus."]]
svg.title: Transmembrane and intracellular receptors
svg.desc: A transmembrane receptor with hydrophobic amino acids in the membrane and hydrophilic amino acids outside binds a hydrophilic peptide ligand that stays outside; a hydrophobic steroid crosses the membrane and binds an intracellular receptor, and the complex enters the nucleus.
svg.text: Blue = hydrophilic amino acids; orange = hydrophobic.

g.data-info: Spans the plasma membrane. Hydrophobic amino acids (orange) are in the region inside the membrane; hydrophilic amino acids (blue) are in the parts in the watery fluid on each side.
Peptides and amines cannot cross the hydrophobic core of the membrane, so they bind a transmembrane receptor and stay outside.
Steroids pass straight through the phospholipid bilayer.
In the cytoplasm or nucleus; hydrophilic throughout. The steroid binds it inside the cell.
The hormone–receptor complex can move into the nucleus and act on genes.
